speaker: Doctor
text: Can you tell me where exactly you feel the pain and when it started?

speaker: Patient
text: 34-year-old female. The patient reports experiencing pain in her right thumb and wrist, which radiates to her elbow for the past three months. The pain worsens when she holds her infant son and is alleviated somewhat with an ice pack. She mentions a history of falling on her right outstretched hand about six months ago. She also notes that her mother has a history of chronic joint pain treated with methotrexate. The patient has been taking ibuprofen as needed for her symptoms.

speaker: Doctor

text: Past medical history: Previous fall on right outstretched hand six months ago. No significant other medical history. Social history: Patient is a mother of an infant, leading a relatively active lifestyle. Does not smoke or consume alcohol regularly.

speaker: Patient
text: Denies any fever, weight loss, or other joint problems. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Gastroenteritis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: That previous diagnosis of gastroenteritis does not explain your wrist pain or the radiating symptoms; those are likely unrelated or incorrect. Given your history of a fall and pain radiating from the thumb to the elbow, I need to check for a scaphoid fracture or ganglion cyst. REQUEST TEST: MRI_Wrist. REQUEST IMAGES: MRI_Wrist. Does pressing firmly on the anatomical snuffbox (the hollow area on the back of your wrist) cause sharp pain?

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: De Quervain's tenosynovitis. While your history of a fall and radiating pain initially suggested a scaphoid fracture, the normal MRI and your mother's rheumatoid arthritis history point more strongly toward an inflammatory or overuse etiology affecting the first dorsal compartment tendons, exacerbated by holding your infant. I will perform a physical exam test known as Finkelstein's maneuver to confirm this.
